## Purpose and Entry Points
Git is a native, distributed version-control system. Its primary executable is the `git` command dispatcher in `git.c`, initialized through `common-main.c` and repository setup in `setup.c`. It routes porcelain and plumbing subcommands to built-ins or external helpers; command registration is represented by `command-list.txt`.

## Command Dispatch and Repository Context
The dispatcher parses global options, locates a repository/worktree, loads configuration, then invokes a selected command implementation. Built-ins cover user-facing workflows and low-level operations under `builtin/`; they share common repository, object, reference, index, and revision APIs.
Paths: `git.c`, `builtin.h`, `builtin/commit.c`, `repository.c`, `config.c`.

## Object Database and Storage Formats
Git’s durable data boundary is the repository’s object database: content-addressed blobs, trees, commits, and tags. Object access abstracts loose-object files, packed object files, and in-memory sources; hashes support SHA-1 and SHA-256. Packfiles, bitmap indexes, commit graphs, and multi-pack indexes provide scalable object lookup, traversal, transfer, and maintenance.
Paths: `object.c`, `object-file.c`, `odb/`, `packfile.c`, `commit-graph.c`, `sha256/`.

## Index, Working Tree, and Change Materialization
The index is the staging/cache layer between filesystem state and tree objects. Commands such as add, checkout, reset, merge, and status reconcile index entries, working-tree paths, attributes, filters, locks, and sparse-checkout rules. Checkout can execute file materialization in parallel.
Paths: `read-cache.c`, `unpack-trees.c`, `checkout.c`, `parallel-checkout.c`, `attr.c`, `convert.c`.

## Refs, History, and Revision Algorithms
Refs name object IDs and are stored through a ref-store abstraction with files, packed-refs, and reftable backends. Commit graph traversal and reachability power log, revision selection, merge-base, blame, and history-aware commands. Reflogs record ref updates; transactions protect atomic reference mutations.
Paths: `refs.c`, `refs/files-backend.c`, `refs/reftable-backend.c`, `reftable/`, `revision.c`, `commit-reach.c`.

## Collaboration, Protocols, and Server Modes
Fetch, push, clone, and remote commands use transport and protocol layers to exchange refs and packed objects. Supported boundaries include local paths, Git native protocol, SSH-mediated execution, HTTP(S) via cURL, and extensible remote helpers. Server-side entry points include upload-pack, receive-pack, HTTP backend, and daemon; credential and hook subsystems mediate authentication and policy.
Paths: `transport.c`, `protocol.c`, `connect.c`, `fetch-pack.c`, `send-pack.c`, `upload-pack.c`, `http-backend.c`, `credential.c`.

## User Workflows, Extensibility, and Runtimes
High-level commands compose the core layers for commit, diff, merge, rebase, stash, archive, maintenance, and submodules. Merge/replay operations persist temporary sequencing state and invoke configurable hooks or external tools. The core runtime is portable C, with shell, Perl, Python, and Tcl components for selected commands/UI integrations; Rust is used for a small library subset.
Paths: `builtin/merge.c`, `merge-ort.c`, `sequencer.c`, `rebase.c`, `hook.c`, `git-submodule.sh`, `git-gui/`, `src/lib.rs`.

## Build, Portability, and Operational Infrastructure
Autoconf/Make is the primary build path, with Meson and contributed CMake support. Platform compatibility layers target Unix, macOS, Windows/MinGW, and MSVC. External build dependencies include cURL, OpenSSL, zlib, expat, and PCRE2; Meson wraps are declared under `subprojects/`. CI runs GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Cirrus configurations.
Paths: `Makefile`, `configure.ac`, `meson.build`, `compat/`, `subprojects/`, `.github/workflows/main.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.cirrus.yml`.
